preamble: Fronting and unrounding of the close back rounded vowel [u] to [i]. It is usually tied to a context. In early Latin, short u became i between l and a labial (lubet > libet). In Southern (Polish and Galician) Yiddish, the u vowel was fronted to i (kugl > kigl). Many other apparent cases, such as Greek υ, went through an intermediate front rounded [y]. Those belong in the u > y and y > i cells.

examples.note: Regular change of /u/ to /i/ next to /l/ and a labial consonant; compare clupeus > clipeus 'shield', lubīdō > libīdō 'desire'.
Southern Yiddish has /i/ wherever Northern and Standard Yiddish have /u/.

sources: Weiss, M. (2009). Outline of the Historical and Comparative Grammar of Latin. Beech Stave Press. https://classics.cornell.edu/outline-historical-and-comparative-grammar-latin
Jacobs, N. G. (2005). Yiddish: A Linguistic Introduction. Cambridge University Press. https://www.cambridge.org/9780521772150
